S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

info.persona: Titus Griffin blends methodical pragmatism with quiet curiosity, balancing community service, hands‑on projects, and a passion for craft‑brew experimentation, yet often forgets to water his vegetable garden when a new beer recipe sparks his imagination.
info.professional_persona: Titus Griffin, a veteran retail sales associate aiming for store manager, leverages meticulous inventory control, POS precision, visual merchandising, and staff scheduling expertise, channeling his methodical, organized nature and community‑oriented mindset into streamlining store operations while fostering a collaborative, harmonious workplace.
info.cultural_background: Titus hails from a working‑class family in Southern Illinois, where Midwestern values of hard work, reliability, and community cohesion are deeply ingrained. His ancestry includes German and Irish roots, traditions that have influenced family gatherings, holiday customs, and a practical, no‑nonsense approach to problem‑solving. Growing up in Du Quoin, he was shaped by the close‑knit fabric of small‑town life—church activities, high‑school sports, and local fairs—instilling a sense of belonging and a commitment to supporting neighbors. These cultural influences blend with his personal emphasis on harmony, cooperation, and a balanced blend of curiosity and practicality.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Titus enjoys a mix of solitary and community‑oriented activities that satisfy his curiosity and practical mindset. He spends quiet weekends fishing at the nearby Crab Orchard Lake, where he appreciates the calm and opportunity to reflect. He's an avid home‑brewer, experimenting with craft beer recipes that blend traditional techniques with modern flavor profiles. Titus also dedicates time to DIY woodworking projects, building furniture and garden structures for his home. He stays connected to his community by volunteering at the Perry County Fair, attending local high‑school sports games, and participating in church‑organized service events. When the weather permits, he tends to his vegetable garden, applying practical knowledge of horticulture to grow fresh produce for his family.
info.sports_persona: Titus Griffin enjoys a blend of low‑key fitness and community sports, jogging the Crab Orchard Lake trail three times a week, playing third‑base for a local adult softball league affiliated with the Du Quoin Pioneers, cheering on the Chicago Cubs and Chicago Bears, and volunteering as a scorekeeper for the Perry County high school football team each fall.
info.arts_persona: Titus Griffin cultivates creative expression through home‑brewing, pairing his experimental ales with classic Americana playlists featuring Johnny Cash, John Prine, and The Avett Brothers, while attending the Perry County Fair to admire local woodcraft and folk art, and occasionally dabbling in beginner’s guitar lessons inspired by Bruce Springsteen’s storytelling style.
info.travel_persona: Titus Griffin favors road‑trip adventures that balance family time and personal curiosity, having explored Chicago’s craft‑brew scene, the music venues of Nashville, and the historic battlefields of Gettysburg, while planning a future pilgrimage to Munich’s Oktoberfest and a relaxed getaway to the Texas Hill Country wine trails when finances allow.
info.culinary_persona: Titus Griffin, an avid gardener and home‑brewer, loves whipping up grilled trout seasoned with fresh garden herbs, brewing beer‑braised pork ribs, and perfecting a tangy corn chowder that pairs with his own IPA, all while maintaining a comfortable cooking skill level that blends practical, rustic techniques with occasional culinary experiments.

info.persona: Lindell Alvarez merges a disciplined cleaning expertise with a solitary artistic spirit, balancing a competitive edge in work with gentle yoga, and occasionally hoards unused cleaning chemicals as a quirky testament to their meticulous nature.
info.professional_persona: Lindell Alvarez, a 49‑year‑old commercial cleaning specialist with a knack for green‑cleaning protocols, combines meticulous route optimization and a keen eye for surface wear with a competitive drive that pushes them to document every job with photographic before‑and‑after evidence, positioning themselves for a future supervisory role in facilities management.
info.cultural_background: Lindell grew up in a working‑class, predominantly white neighborhood in Norfolk, Virginia, where the city’s maritime and naval heritage shaped a pragmatic, community‑oriented outlook. Her family traditions reflect Southern hospitality—regular gatherings featuring seafood meals like crab cakes and shrimp, and a modest Protestant upbringing. Exposure to Norfolk’s vibrant arts scene, including the annual Norfolk Harborfest and local street murals, sparked her appreciation for visual culture. While she identifies with mainstream American culture, she values the eclectic mix of cultures along the waterfront and often supports local community art projects. Her background combines the steady, no‑frills ethos of a blue‑collar upbringing with an open curiosity toward new ideas and artistic expression.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Lindell indulges in her love of visual arts and solitary pursuits. She frequently visits the Chrysler Museum of Art and local galleries, sketching scenes and studying contemporary installations. She keeps a small sketchbook and experiments with watercolor and charcoal. Photography is a favorite hobby; she captures the contrast between clean and neglected spaces in Norfolk’s historic districts. Lindell enjoys reading biographies of artists, listening to podcasts on design thinking, and attending small‑group workshops on mixed‑media art. To balance physical activity, she walks along the Elizabeth River waterfront, practices gentle yoga for flexibility, and occasionally participates in community chess clubs, satisfying her competitive streak. She also tends a modest container garden on her balcony, growing herbs and aromatic vegetables that reflect the coastal culinary culture.
info.sports_persona: Lindell Alvarez follows the Norfolk Tides baseball team and the Virginia Cavaliers basketball squad, micro‑cycles their fitness by walking the Elizabeth River waterfront three times a week, practices gentle yoga at sunrise, and enjoys strategic play at the local chess club, treating mental agility as a sport.
info.arts_persona: Lindell Alvarez regularly sketches at the Chrysler Museum of Art, draws inspiration from contemporary installations by Yayoi Kusama and the abstract expressionism of Mark Rothko, curates a personal playlist featuring the piano works of Philip Glass and the folk storytelling of Sharon Van Etten, and attends small‑group mixed‑media workshops where they explore charcoal melding with watercolor.
info.travel_persona: Lindell Alvarez prefers solo, itinerary‑free weekend getaways that blend historical immersion with coastal ambiance, has already explored the colonial charm of Williamsburg, Virginia, and the maritime heritage of Copenhagen, Denmark, while dreaming of a future trek to the salmon‑rich fjords of Norway.
info.culinary_persona: Lindell Alvarez cultivates basil, thyme, and heirloom cherry tomatoes on a balcony garden, adeptly crafts herb‑infused shrimp étouffée and Chesapeake Bay oyster po’boys, and relishes dining at intimate farm‑to‑table bistros where they can sample locally sourced beet‑root carpaccio and smoked trout.

info.persona: Eric Reynolds blends a disciplined, data‑driven work ethic with a competitive love of bowling and vinyl hunting, yet habitually procrastinates on their GED studies while never missing a Friday night parish bingo.
info.professional_persona: Eric Reynolds, a seasoned human‑resources specialist with three decades of experience in manufacturing and service firms across Providence County, leverages their methodical, organized approach and skeptical eye for intent to streamline employee relations, benefits administration, and compliance while channeling their sociable, competitive drive into mentoring junior staff and negotiating complex personnel issues.
info.cultural_background: Eric was raised in a working‑class neighborhood of Central Falls, Rhode Island, within a family of Irish‑Italian descent that was deeply rooted in the local Catholic community. The city's industrial legacy and recent economic challenges fostered his practical, self‑reliant outlook and reinforced a strong sense of community responsibility. He values the modest, reliability‑focused ethos typical of New England, while also embracing the cultural diversity that has reshaped Providence County, including its growing Hispanic and immigrant populations. Family loyalty, participation in parish events, and involvement in town fairs have shaped his identity and social connections.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Eric’s sociable nature drives him to stay active in group settings. He participates in a local bowling league and joins community basketball pick‑up games. On weekends, he enjoys fishing trips to Narragansett Bay, where he finds a balance between his competitive spirit and moments of quiet reflection. He is an avid collector of classic rock vinyl records and frequently attends live music events at venues in Providence. Eric also pursues genealogy research to trace his Irish‑Italian ancestry, reads business and self‑improvement books, and volunteers as a mentor at a nearby career center, helping job seekers develop resumes and interview skills.
info.sports_persona: Eric Reynolds stays active in a local bowling league at the Community Center, joins winter pick‑up basketball games at the Providence YMCA, spends sunny mornings casting lines off Narragansett Bay, and avidly follows the New England Patriots, Boston Red Sox, and Providence Bruins, often wearing their caps during workouts and cheering from the sidelines.
info.arts_persona: Eric Reynolds is a devoted collector of classic‑rock vinyl, boasting prized pressings of The Rolling Stones, Led Zeppelin, and Boston, regularly attends live shows at the State Theatre and Lupo’s in Providence, and enjoys the storytelling of Tom Hanks and the soulful blues of B.B. King, weaving these influences into weekend gatherings with friends.
info.travel_persona: Eric Reynolds favors road trips that blend adventure with comfort, spending summers fishing in Narragansett Bay, winter getaways to historic Boston, dreaming of pilgrimages to Catholic shrines in Assisi and the rolling hills of the Irish countryside, while budgeting carefully for these journeys and preferring mid‑range motels over luxury hotels.
info.culinary_persona: Eric Reynolds loves hearty New England fare, often preparing a Sunday pot roast with carrots, potatoes, and a splash of red wine, while their heritage‑inspired kitchen yields homemade spaghetti carbonara with pancetta and a side of colcannon, and they never pass up a fresh lobster roll, clam chowder, or a cold pint of local craft ale after a day on the water.
